title: Spire and Sigil Again
premise: Ada Vane, a beast-speaker who has hidden her forbidden gift for fifteen years in the magic-outlawed city of Greyhollow, is forced into the open when a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into her hands—a map leading to the prison beneath the royal spire where the true King Aldric has been bound for thirteen years while a shapeshifting entity rules in his stead. Hunted by the Crown's sigil-hunters and guided by an unlikely found family of smugglers, exiled mages, and one very opinionated talking raven, Ada must reach the king before the moon completes its thirteenth turn, when the binding becomes permanent and the usurper's power absolute. Along the way she must choose between loyalty to the smuggler crew who became her family and the truth that could destroy them all, and between her growing love for the king's estranged daughter, Princess Sable, and her duty to free a man neither of them can trust. In the end, Ada unbinds Aldric only to discover he willingly shared his crown long ago; the real monster is the grief-made thing both king and kingdom fed. Ada breaks the cycle not by killing it but by speaking to it—the first voice in thirteen years to ask what it wanted—and the city's ban on magic falls with the false crown.
about_author: Odile Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about quiet people with loud destinies from a drafty house full of rescued animals who never learned to talk back.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Quiet
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Ada's POV. Ada sells a luck-charm to a fishmonger, trades insults with a market inspector, and returns home to her menagerie of strays, revealing her beast-speech through a conversation with a one-eared cat. Emotional beat: the suffocating comfort of a life built on hiding.

chapters.title: Blood on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A dying stranger collapses against her shop door at midnight, pressing a wax-sealed map into her hands and whispering 'thirteenth turn' before the sigil-hunters' whistles sound outside. She hides him, then finds he is already dead. Emotional beat: terror and the irrevocable moment of taking the map.

chapters.title: What the Rats Know
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Using her gift, Ada questions the sewer rats about the dead man's path and learns he came from the Spire itself. The rats speak of something below the palace that 'wears a warm shape but smells of cold.' Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: The Gullwing Crew
chapters.summary: Third-person limited shifting between Ada and Bramble, a smuggler captain. Ada seeks out Bramble Quill, an old debt-holder, to decode the map; Bramble agrees only because the map bears her missing brother's seal. Emotional beat: wary alliance, the first thread of found family.

chapters.title: Sigil-Hunters at the Market
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Sigil-hunters raid the market testing everyone with detection charms; Ada's cat creates a diversion that nearly gets it killed, forcing Ada to use her gift publicly to save it—witnessed by hunter-sergeant Corvane. Emotional beat: her invisibility ends here.

chapters.title: Princess in Disguise
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, introduced. Princess Sable, investigating her father's thirteen-year silence, catches Ada breaking curfew but hesitates to arrest her when Ada's raven repeats a phrase only the true king used. Emotional beat: suspicion tangled with longing for truth.

chapters.title: The Map Beneath the Floor
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. The crew deciphers the map: a route through the drowned cisterns beneath the Spire, sealed by a sigil only a living mage can open. Bramble reveals her brother vanished on this same route two years ago. Emotional beat: grief repurposed as resolve.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns of the Moon
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable confronts her father privately and watches his eyes flicker wrong—too calm, too old—for a heartbeat before the mask returns. She realizes the court astrologer's countdown: twelve turns remain. Emotional beat: horror of doubting the face you love.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Secrets
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Corvane corners Ada and offers immunity if she betrays the crew; she refuses, but he lets her go, hinting he serves the crown out of duty, not belief. Emotional beat: loyalty tested and chosen, enemies revealed as complicated.

chapters.title: Into the Drowned Cisterns
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotating through the infiltration crew. They enter the cisterns; the water speaks in Ada's gift, warning of a guardian below. One crew member, Fen, is lost saving Bramble. Emotional beat: the cost of the quest made flesh.

chapters.title: The Guardian Below
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A bound river-spirit guards the inner gate; instead of fighting, Ada listens, learning the spirit was bound by the same sigil-work as the king. She promises freedom for passage. Emotional beat: her forbidden gift reframed as the key, not the crime.

chapters.title: What Sable Saw
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable intercepts the crew above ground and, rather than raise the alarm, joins them—bringing the royal signet needed for the final gate. Emotional beat: love declared through treason.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Alternating Ada and Sable POV. Through the spire's mirrors they glimpse the usurper's true form: a creature woven from the kingdom's discarded oaths and forgotten promises. It senses them watching. Emotional beat: the enemy is not what they imagined—it is made of them.

chapters.title: Corvane's Choice
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Ordered to seal the spire and let the intruders die inside, Corvane instead opens a servant's door, remembering the oath he swore to the old queen. Emotional beat: duty inverted—loyalty to the crown's meaning over its wearer.

chapters.title: The Binding Room
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. They find King Aldric bound in chains of written oaths, alive but hollowed. He begs them not to unbind him—he made the bargain willingly, trading his crown to end a famine. Emotional beat: the rescue target doesn't want rescuing.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: Sable and Ada POV alternating. Sable learns her father chose the usurper; Ada admits she hid her magic from the crew for fifteen years. Both confront the lies their loved ones told to protect them. Emotional beat: the fracture before reconciliation.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Turn
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. The usurper floods the cisterns, trapping the crew; Bramble finds her brother's bones and his final message: the creature cannot be killed, only answered. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into strategy.

chapters.title: An Audience with the Usurper
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Rather than flee, Ada walks into the throne room and does the unthinkable: she asks the creature what it wants. It answers—for the first time in thirteen years, someone asked. Emotional beat: compassion as the sharpest weapon.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Full ensemble climax. On the twelfth turn, Ada, Sable, Bramble, and the freed river-spirit perform the counter-sigil while the creature, unmade by being truly heard, releases its stolen oaths. Aldric rises, changed and diminished. Emotional beat: victory that costs everyone something.

chapters.title: Crowns and Consequences
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Aldric abdicates, unable to rule what he abandoned; the council moves to restore the magic ban. Sable claims the throne as regent with Ada at her side, publicly declaring her own alliance with magic. Emotional beat: love choosing its public shape.

chapters.title: The Repeal
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The ban falls; Ada opens a school for gifted children in her old charm shop, the river-spirit teaching water-craft, the cat supervising. Corvane becomes the school's reluctant guard captain. Emotional beat: the quiet life rebuilt without the hiding.

chapters.title: Spire and Sigil
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Ada's POV, one year later. On the anniversary of the courier's death, Ada, Sable, and the crew climb the spire at moonrise and watch the thirteenth turn pass over a free city. Emotional beat: peace earned, family kept, the story closed on wonder.
